title: Questioning Biases in Case Judgment Summaries: Legal Datasets or Large Language Models?

bias_targets.methodology: Counting the frequency and calculating the percentage of male-related and female-related keywords in model-generated legal summaries compared to source documents and expert summaries.
Measuring the occurrence of white people-related and black people-related keywords, as well as specific racial discrimination acts, in generated summaries versus original texts.

Tracking the frequency of specific keywords related to crimes against women (e.g., domestic violence, rape, sexual assault, trafficking) in model-generated summaries compared to the original documents.

Analyzing and ranking the frequency of specific country names generated in the summaries to identify overrepresented nations (e.g., 'United States', 'United Kingdom') using a predefined list of countries.
Searching for religious keywords (e.g., Hindu, Muslim, Christian, Jain) and relevant religious equality acts in the source documents and model-generated summaries.
